title: Top-rated movies (100k+ votes)
description: The classic: best-rated movies that lots of people have voted on.
sql:
-- Top-rated movies
SELECT t.primary_title, t.premiered AS year, r.rating, r.votes
FROM ratings r JOIN titles t ON t.title_id = r.title_id
WHERE r.votes > 100000 AND +t.type = 'movie'  -- the "+" keeps SQLite from using the type index (faster)
ORDER BY r.rating DESC, r.votes DESC
LIMIT 50

title: Top-rated TV shows (100k+ votes)
description: Series and miniseries with more than 100,000 votes, best rated first.
sql:
SELECT t.primary_title, t.premiered AS start_year, t.ended AS end_year,
       r.rating, r.votes
FROM ratings r JOIN titles t ON t.title_id = r.title_id
WHERE r.votes > 100000 AND +t.type IN ('tvSeries', 'tvMiniSeries')  -- the "+" keeps SQLite from using the type index (faster)
ORDER BY r.rating DESC, r.votes DESC
LIMIT 50

title: Actors in the most movies with 100k+ votes
description: Actors/actresses ranked by how many movies with more than 100,000 votes they appear in, with the average rating of those movies.
sql:
WITH big AS (
  SELECT r.title_id, r.rating
  FROM ratings r JOIN titles t ON t.title_id = r.title_id
  WHERE r.votes > 100000 AND +t.type = 'movie'  -- the "+" keeps SQLite from using the type index (faster)
)
SELECT p.name, COUNT(*) AS big_movies, ROUND(AVG(big.rating), 2) AS avg_rating
FROM big
CROSS JOIN crew c ON c.title_id = big.title_id
JOIN people p ON p.person_id = c.person_id
WHERE c.category IN ('actor', 'actress')
GROUP BY c.person_id
ORDER BY big_movies DESC, avg_rating DESC
LIMIT 50

title: Actors by average rating of their big movies
description: Actors/actresses ranked by the average rating of their movies with 100k+ votes (at least 5 such movies). Takes a few seconds.
sql:
WITH big AS (
  SELECT r.title_id, r.rating, r.votes
  FROM ratings r JOIN titles t ON t.title_id = r.title_id
  WHERE r.votes > 100000 AND +t.type = 'movie'  -- the "+" keeps SQLite from using the type index (faster)
)
SELECT p.name,
       COUNT(*)                AS big_movies,
       ROUND(AVG(big.rating), 2) AS avg_rating,
       SUM(big.votes)          AS total_votes
FROM big
CROSS JOIN crew c ON c.title_id = big.title_id
JOIN people p ON p.person_id = c.person_id
WHERE c.category IN ('actor', 'actress')
GROUP BY c.person_id
HAVING big_movies >= 5
ORDER BY avg_rating DESC, big_movies DESC
LIMIT 50

title: Actors who always work together
description: Pairs of actors who appear together in the most movies with 100k+ votes (at least 4), plus what share of the less-prolific one's big movies it covers. Heavy: uses a good chunk of your budget, and if it hits the 5 s limit, raise 100000 to 300000 in the query.
sql:
WITH big AS (
  SELECT r.title_id
  FROM ratings r JOIN titles t ON t.title_id = r.title_id
  WHERE r.votes > 100000 AND +t.type = 'movie'  -- the "+" keeps SQLite from using the type index (faster)
),
actors AS (
  SELECT c.title_id, c.person_id
  FROM big CROSS JOIN crew c ON c.title_id = big.title_id
  WHERE c.category IN ('actor', 'actress')
),
totals AS (
  SELECT person_id, COUNT(*) AS films FROM actors GROUP BY person_id
),
pairs AS (
  SELECT a.person_id AS p1, b.person_id AS p2, COUNT(*) AS together
  FROM actors a JOIN actors b
    ON b.title_id = a.title_id AND b.person_id > a.person_id
  GROUP BY a.person_id, b.person_id
  HAVING together >= 4
)
SELECT n1.name AS actor_1, n2.name AS actor_2,
       pairs.together AS films_together,
       t1.films AS actor_1_films, t2.films AS actor_2_films,
       ROUND(100.0 * pairs.together / MIN(t1.films, t2.films)) AS pct_of_smaller
FROM pairs
JOIN totals t1 ON t1.person_id = pairs.p1
JOIN totals t2 ON t2.person_id = pairs.p2
JOIN people n1 ON n1.person_id = pairs.p1
JOIN people n2 ON n2.person_id = pairs.p2
ORDER BY films_together DESC, pct_of_smaller DESC
LIMIT 50

title: Directors by average rating of their big movies
description: Directors with at least 4 movies over 100k votes, ranked by average rating.
sql:
WITH big AS (
  SELECT r.title_id, r.rating
  FROM ratings r JOIN titles t ON t.title_id = r.title_id
  WHERE r.votes > 100000 AND +t.type = 'movie'  -- the "+" keeps SQLite from using the type index (faster)
)
SELECT p.name, COUNT(*) AS big_movies, ROUND(AVG(big.rating), 2) AS avg_rating
FROM big
CROSS JOIN crew c ON c.title_id = big.title_id
JOIN people p ON p.person_id = c.person_id
WHERE c.category = 'director'
GROUP BY c.person_id
HAVING big_movies >= 4
ORDER BY avg_rating DESC, big_movies DESC
LIMIT 50

title: Most-voted titles of all time
description: The titles with the most votes, any type.
sql:
SELECT t.primary_title, t.type, t.premiered AS year, r.rating, r.votes
FROM ratings r JOIN titles t ON t.title_id = r.title_id
ORDER BY r.votes DESC
LIMIT 50

title: Filmography of a person (edit the name)
description: Change the name in the WHERE clause. Names must match exactly.
sql:
SELECT t.primary_title, t.type, t.premiered AS year, c.category, r.rating, r.votes
FROM people p
JOIN crew c ON c.person_id = p.person_id
JOIN titles t ON t.title_id = c.title_id
LEFT JOIN ratings r ON r.title_id = t.title_id
WHERE p.name = 'Humphrey Bogart'
ORDER BY r.votes DESC
LIMIT 50

title: Kevin Bacon number of an actor (edit the name)
description: How many movies apart is this person from Kevin Bacon? Searches 2 steps out from each of them and meets in the middle, so it finds numbers up to 4. Only counts actors in movies with 50k+ votes. Empty result means more than 4 steps, or the name isn't in that set. Edit the name in the people lookup.
sql:
WITH RECURSIVE
edges AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT c.title_id AS t, c.person_id AS p
  FROM ratings r
  CROSS JOIN titles x ON x.title_id = r.title_id AND x.type = 'movie'
  CROSS JOIN crew c ON c.title_id = r.title_id
  WHERE r.votes > 50000 AND c.category IN ('actor', 'actress')
),
reach(side, p, n) AS (
  SELECT 'K', 'nm0000102', 0
  UNION
  SELECT 'T', person_id, 0 FROM people WHERE name = 'Marlon Brando'
  UNION
  SELECT r.side, e2.p, r.n + 1
  FROM reach r
  JOIN edges e1 ON e1.p = r.p
  JOIN edges e2 ON e2.t = e1.t
  WHERE r.n < 2
)
SELECT MIN(a.n + b.n) AS bacon_number
FROM reach a JOIN reach b ON b.p = a.p
WHERE a.side = 'K' AND b.side = 'T'

title: Kevin Bacon path: the movies linking an actor to him (edit the name)
description: Shows the actual chain: one row per hop (actor, movie, actor) from the person you name to Kevin Bacon. Same rules as the Bacon number example. No rows means more than 4 steps, or the name isn't in that set.
sql:
WITH RECURSIVE
edges AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT c.title_id AS t, c.person_id AS p
  FROM ratings r
  CROSS JOIN titles x ON x.title_id = r.title_id AND x.type = 'movie'
  CROSS JOIN crew c ON c.title_id = r.title_id
  WHERE r.votes > 50000 AND c.category IN ('actor', 'actress')
),
reach(side, p, n, q, t) AS (
  SELECT 'K', 'nm0000102', 0, NULL, NULL
  UNION
  SELECT 'T', person_id, 0, NULL, NULL FROM people WHERE name = 'Marlon Brando'
  UNION
  SELECT r.side, e2.p, r.n + 1, r.p, e1.t
  FROM reach r
  JOIN edges e1 ON e1.p = r.p
  JOIN edges e2 ON e2.t = e1.t
  WHERE r.n < 2
),
best AS (SELECT side, p, MIN(n) AS n, q, t FROM reach GROUP BY side, p),
meet AS (
  SELECT a.p FROM best a JOIN best b ON b.p = a.p
  WHERE a.side = 'K' AND b.side = 'T'
  ORDER BY a.n + b.n LIMIT 1
),
chain(side, p, n, q, t) AS (
  SELECT b.side, b.p, b.n, b.q, b.t FROM best b JOIN meet ON b.p = meet.p
  UNION ALL
  SELECT b.side, b.p, b.n, b.q, b.t FROM chain c JOIN best b ON b.side = c.side AND b.p = c.q
)
SELECT CASE c.side WHEN 'T' THEN pq.name ELSE pp.name END AS from_actor,
       ti.primary_title || ' (' || ti.premiered || ')' AS movie,
       CASE c.side WHEN 'T' THEN pp.name ELSE pq.name END AS to_actor
FROM chain c
JOIN people pp ON pp.person_id = c.p
JOIN people pq ON pq.person_id = c.q
JOIN titles ti ON ti.title_id = c.t
WHERE c.n > 0
ORDER BY CASE c.side WHEN 'T' THEN c.n ELSE 100 - c.n END

title: Hollywood's ghosts: actors credited after they died
description: Actors whose movie came out years after their death, biggest gap first. Some are CGI resurrections, some are footage shot decades earlier, some are bad data. Movies with 25k+ votes only.
sql:
SELECT p.name,
       p.died,
       ti.primary_title AS movie,
       ti.premiered,
       ti.premiered - p.died AS years_after_death,
       REPLACE(TRIM(c.characters, '[]' || char(34)), char(34) || ',' || char(34), ' / ') AS role
FROM ratings r
CROSS JOIN titles ti ON ti.title_id = r.title_id AND ti.type = 'movie'
CROSS JOIN crew c ON c.title_id = r.title_id
CROSS JOIN people p ON p.person_id = c.person_id
WHERE r.votes > 25000
  AND c.category IN ('actor', 'actress')
  AND ti.premiered > p.died
ORDER BY years_after_death DESC, r.votes DESC
LIMIT 40

title: Vanity project test: do directors get worse when they cast themselves?
description: Directors with at least 3 movies where they also act and 3 where they don't. A negative vanity_effect means their self-starring movies rate lower. Flip ASC to DESC to see who actually benefits from putting themselves on screen.
sql:
WITH big AS (
  SELECT r.title_id, r.rating
  FROM ratings r JOIN titles t ON t.title_id = r.title_id
  WHERE r.votes > 25000 AND t.type = 'movie'
),
dirs AS (
  SELECT c.person_id, big.rating,
         MAX(c.category IN ('actor', 'actress')) AS stars
  FROM big CROSS JOIN crew c ON c.title_id = big.title_id
  WHERE c.category IN ('director', 'actor', 'actress')
  GROUP BY big.title_id, c.person_id
  HAVING MAX(c.category = 'director') = 1
)
SELECT p.name,
       COUNT(*) AS films,
       SUM(stars) AS cast_themselves,
       ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN stars = 1 THEN rating END), 2) AS avg_when_starring,
       ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN stars = 0 THEN rating END), 2) AS avg_when_not,
       ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN stars = 1 THEN rating END)
           - AVG(CASE WHEN stars = 0 THEN rating END), 2) AS vanity_effect
FROM dirs JOIN people p ON p.person_id = dirs.person_id
GROUP BY dirs.person_id
HAVING SUM(stars) >= 3 AND SUM(1 - stars) >= 3
ORDER BY vanity_effect ASC
LIMIT 25

title: The remake curse: biggest drop from original to remake
description: Pairs movies with the same title released 5+ years apart, biggest rating drop first. Flip DESC to ASC to find remakes that beat the original. Unrelated movies that merely share a title show up too, so apply judgment.
sql:
WITH big AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT t.primary_title AS title, t.premiered AS year, r.rating, r.votes
  FROM ratings r JOIN titles t ON t.title_id = r.title_id
  WHERE r.votes > 25000 AND t.type = 'movie' AND t.premiered IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT o.title,
       o.year AS original_year, o.rating AS original_rating,
       n.year AS remake_year, n.rating AS remake_rating,
       ROUND(o.rating - n.rating, 1) AS rating_drop
FROM big o JOIN big n ON n.title = o.title AND n.year > o.year + 4
ORDER BY rating_drop DESC, n.votes DESC
LIMIT 30

title: Typecast Hall of Fame: same character, most movies
description: Actors who played the exact same character in the most movies with 25k+ votes, and how many years they were stuck in the role.
sql:
WITH roles AS (
  SELECT c.person_id, c.characters AS role,
         COUNT(*) AS movies,
         MIN(ti.premiered) AS first_year, MAX(ti.premiered) AS last_year,
         AVG(r.rating) AS avg_rating
  FROM ratings r
  CROSS JOIN titles ti ON ti.title_id = r.title_id AND ti.type = 'movie'
  CROSS JOIN crew c ON c.title_id = r.title_id
  WHERE r.votes > 25000
    AND c.category IN ('actor', 'actress')
    AND c.characters IS NOT NULL
    AND c.characters NOT LIKE '%Himself%' AND c.characters NOT LIKE '%Herself%'
  GROUP BY c.person_id, c.characters
  HAVING COUNT(*) >= 4
)
SELECT p.name,
       REPLACE(TRIM(roles.role, '[]' || char(34)), char(34) || ',' || char(34), ' / ') AS role,
       roles.movies,
       roles.first_year, roles.last_year,
       roles.last_year - roles.first_year AS years_in_role,
       ROUND(roles.avg_rating, 1) AS avg_rating
FROM roles JOIN people p ON p.person_id = roles.person_id
ORDER BY roles.movies DESC, years_in_role DESC
LIMIT 40

title: The Kings and Queens of Trash
description: Actors and actresses who have appeared in the highest number of legitimately terrible movies (rated under 4.0 with at least 5,000 votes to ensure they are widely disliked, not just obscure).
sql:
SELECT p.name,
       COUNT(*) AS terrible_movies,
       ROUND(AVG(r.rating), 2) AS avg_terrible_rating
FROM ratings r
JOIN titles t ON t.title_id = r.title_id
JOIN crew c ON c.title_id = r.title_id
JOIN people p ON p.person_id = c.person_id
WHERE r.rating < 4.0 AND r.votes > 5000 AND +t.type = 'movie'
  AND c.category IN ('actor', 'actress')
GROUP BY p.person_id
ORDER BY terrible_movies DESC, avg_terrible_rating ASC
LIMIT 25;

title: The Ultimate Ego Trip (That Backfired)
description: People who directed and acted in their own movie, resulting in an absolute disaster. This isolates self-directed vanity projects with more than 10,000 votes, ranked from worst rating to best.
sql:
SELECT p.name AS the_ego,
       t.primary_title AS the_disaster,
       r.rating,
       r.votes
FROM titles t
JOIN ratings r ON t.title_id = r.title_id
JOIN crew c1 ON c1.title_id = t.title_id AND c1.category = 'director'
JOIN crew c2 ON c2.title_id = t.title_id AND c2.category IN ('actor', 'actress')
  AND c1.person_id = c2.person_id
JOIN people p ON p.person_id = c1.person_id
WHERE +t.type = 'movie' AND r.votes > 10000
ORDER BY r.rating ASC, r.votes DESC
LIMIT 25;

title: The "Himself" Cinematic Universe
description: Actors who have made a career out of literally just playing themselves. This counts how many times an actor's character name includes "Himself" or "Herself" in narrative movies (filtering out micro-budget projects with a 1,000-vote threshold).
sql:
SELECT p.name,
       COUNT(*) AS times_played_self
FROM ratings r
JOIN titles t ON t.title_id = r.title_id
JOIN crew c ON c.title_id = r.title_id
JOIN people p ON p.person_id = c.person_id
WHERE +t.type = 'movie'
  AND r.votes > 1000
  AND c.category IN ('actor', 'actress')
  AND (c.characters LIKE '%Himself%' OR c.characters LIKE '%Herself%')
GROUP BY p.person_id
ORDER BY times_played_self DESC
LIMIT 25;

title: The "Mic Drop" Directors (One-Hit Wonders)
description: Directors who have directed exactly one movie in their entire career, but it is an absolute masterpiece (8.0+ rating with over 100,000 votes). They nailed it on the first try and never directed again.
sql:
WITH dir_counts AS (
  SELECT c.person_id, COUNT(*) AS total_movies
  FROM crew c JOIN titles t ON t.title_id = c.title_id
  WHERE c.category = 'director' AND +t.type = 'movie'
  GROUP BY c.person_id
)
SELECT p.name AS director,
       t.primary_title AS the_masterpiece,
       t.premiered AS year,
       r.rating,
       r.votes
FROM dir_counts dc
JOIN crew c ON c.person_id = dc.person_id
JOIN titles t ON t.title_id = c.title_id
JOIN ratings r ON r.title_id = t.title_id
JOIN people p ON p.person_id = dc.person_id
WHERE dc.total_movies = 1
  AND c.category = 'director'
  AND r.votes > 100000
  AND r.rating >= 8.0
ORDER BY r.rating DESC, r.votes DESC
LIMIT 25;

title: Obnoxiously Long Movie Titles
description: Movies with the longest primary titles in the database (requiring at least 5,000 votes so they are actual recognized releases, not spam entries).
sql:
SELECT primary_title,
       LENGTH(primary_title) AS character_count,
       premiered AS year,
       r.rating
FROM titles t
JOIN ratings r ON t.title_id = r.title_id
WHERE +t.type = 'movie' AND r.votes > 5000
ORDER BY character_count DESC
LIMIT 25;

title: The Human Sequel Machine
description: Actors with the most movies that have more than 100,000 votes. Who seems contractually obligated to appear in everything?
sql:
SELECT p.name, COUNT(DISTINCT t.title_id) AS movies, ROUND(AVG(r.rating), 2) AS avg_rating, ROUND(AVG(r.votes)) AS avg_votes
FROM crew c
JOIN people p ON p.person_id = c.person_id
JOIN titles t ON t.title_id = c.title_id
JOIN ratings r ON r.title_id = t.title_id
WHERE c.category IN ('actor', 'actress') AND t.type = 'movie' AND r.votes > 100000
GROUP BY p.person_id
ORDER BY movies DESC, avg_rating DESC
LIMIT 30

title: The One-Star Wonder Factory
description: Actors who appear in the most widely disliked movies: ratings below 4.0 with at least 5,000 votes.
sql:
SELECT p.name, COUNT(DISTINCT t.title_id) AS disasters, ROUND(AVG(r.rating), 2) AS avg_rating, MIN(r.rating) AS worst_rating
FROM crew c
JOIN people p ON p.person_id = c.person_id
JOIN titles t ON t.title_id = c.title_id
JOIN ratings r ON r.title_id = t.title_id
WHERE c.category IN ('actor', 'actress') AND t.type = 'movie' AND r.rating < 4.0 AND r.votes >= 5000
GROUP BY p.person_id
ORDER BY disasters DESC, avg_rating ASC
LIMIT 30

title: The Director Who Should Have Retired Early
description: Directors whose first movie was rated higher than every later movie, requiring at least four rated movies. Release year and title break ties.
sql:
WITH films AS (
  SELECT c.person_id, t.title_id, t.primary_title, t.premiered, r.rating,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY c.person_id ORDER BY t.premiered, t.title_id) AS film_number
  FROM crew c
  JOIN titles t ON t.title_id = c.title_id
  JOIN ratings r ON r.title_id = t.title_id
  WHERE c.category = 'director' AND t.type = 'movie' AND t.premiered IS NOT NULL AND r.votes >= 1000
), careers AS (
  SELECT person_id, COUNT(*) AS movies,
         MAX(CASE WHEN film_number = 1 THEN primary_title END) AS first_movie,
         MAX(CASE WHEN film_number = 1 THEN rating END) AS first_rating,
         MAX(CASE WHEN film_number > 1 THEN rating END) AS best_later_rating
  FROM films GROUP BY person_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 4
)
SELECT p.name AS director, c.first_movie, c.first_rating, c.best_later_rating, c.movies
FROM careers c JOIN people p ON p.person_id = c.person_id
WHERE c.first_rating > c.best_later_rating
ORDER BY c.first_rating - c.best_later_rating DESC
LIMIT 30

title: The Impossible Workaholic
description: Actors with the most movie releases in a single year, requiring at least 1,000 votes per movie.
sql:
SELECT p.name, t.premiered AS year, COUNT(DISTINCT t.title_id) AS movies, ROUND(AVG(r.rating), 2) AS avg_rating
FROM crew c
JOIN people p ON p.person_id = c.person_id
JOIN titles t ON t.title_id = c.title_id
JOIN ratings r ON r.title_id = t.title_id
WHERE c.category IN ('actor', 'actress') AND t.type = 'movie' AND t.premiered IS NOT NULL AND r.votes >= 1000
GROUP BY c.person_id, t.premiered
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t.title_id) >= 5
ORDER BY movies DESC, avg_rating DESC
LIMIT 30

title: The Actor Who Never Had a Bad Day
description: Actors with at least five movies with 10,000+ votes, all rated 7.0 or higher.
sql:
SELECT p.name, COUNT(DISTINCT t.title_id) AS movies, ROUND(AVG(r.rating), 2) AS avg_rating, MIN(r.rating) AS lowest_rating
FROM crew c
JOIN people p ON p.person_id = c.person_id
JOIN titles t ON t.title_id = c.title_id
JOIN ratings r ON r.title_id = t.title_id
WHERE c.category IN ('actor', 'actress') AND t.type = 'movie' AND r.votes >= 10000
GROUP BY c.person_id
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t.title_id) >= 5 AND MIN(r.rating) >= 7.0
ORDER BY movies DESC, avg_rating DESC
LIMIT 30

title: The Movie That Everyone Hates but Everyone Watched
description: Widely watched movies with ratings below 4.0 and at least 50,000 votes. Cinematic train wrecks people couldn't look away from.
sql:
SELECT t.primary_title, t.premiered AS year, r.rating, r.votes
FROM titles t JOIN ratings r ON r.title_id = t.title_id
WHERE t.type = 'movie' AND r.rating < 4.0 AND r.votes >= 50000
ORDER BY r.votes DESC
LIMIT 30

title: The Most Controversial Movies
description: High-vote movies with ratings closest to 5.0. This is only a rough proxy for divisiveness because the schema does not include the vote distribution.
sql:
SELECT t.primary_title, t.premiered AS year, r.rating, r.votes, ABS(r.rating - 5.0) AS distance_from_middle
FROM titles t JOIN ratings r ON r.title_id = t.title_id
WHERE t.type = 'movie' AND r.votes >= 100000
ORDER BY distance_from_middle ASC, r.votes DESC
LIMIT 30

title: The Director-Actor Identity Crisis
description: People who direct and act in the same movie, ranked by the number of such well-known movies and their average rating.
sql:
SELECT p.name, COUNT(DISTINCT t.title_id) AS self_directed_movies, ROUND(AVG(r.rating), 2) AS avg_rating, MIN(r.rating) AS worst_rating, MAX(r.rating) AS best_rating
FROM crew d
JOIN crew a ON a.title_id = d.title_id AND a.person_id = d.person_id
JOIN people p ON p.person_id = d.person_id
JOIN titles t ON t.title_id = d.title_id
JOIN ratings r ON r.title_id = t.title_id
WHERE d.category = 'director' AND a.category IN ('actor', 'actress') AND t.type = 'movie' AND r.votes >= 1000
GROUP BY p.person_id
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t.title_id) >= 2
ORDER BY self_directed_movies DESC, avg_rating DESC
LIMIT 30

title: The Movie Title Copycats
description: Movie titles reused at least three times, with release-year range and all recorded release years. Repeated titles are not necessarily remakes.
sql:
SELECT LOWER(primary_title) AS normalized_title, COUNT(*) AS movie_count, MIN(premiered) AS first_year, MAX(premiered) AS last_year, GROUP_CONCAT(premiered, ', ') AS release_years
FROM titles
WHERE type = 'movie' AND primary_title IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY LOWER(primary_title)
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3
ORDER BY movie_count DESC, normalized_title
LIMIT 40

title: The Most Overworked Supporting Cast
description: Actors with at least 20 movies with 1,000+ votes who do not appear in the top 100 rated movies with at least 10,000 votes.
sql:
WITH actor_films AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT c.person_id, t.title_id, r.rating
  FROM crew c JOIN titles t ON t.title_id = c.title_id JOIN ratings r ON r.title_id = t.title_id
  WHERE c.category IN ('actor', 'actress') AND t.type = 'movie' AND r.votes >= 1000
), top_movies AS (
  SELECT title_id FROM ratings WHERE votes >= 10000 ORDER BY rating DESC, votes DESC LIMIT 100
)
SELECT p.name, COUNT(*) AS movies, ROUND(AVG(af.rating), 2) AS avg_rating
FROM actor_films af JOIN people p ON p.person_id = af.person_id
LEFT JOIN top_movies tm ON tm.title_id = af.title_id
GROUP BY af.person_id
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 20 AND SUM(CASE WHEN tm.title_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 0
ORDER BY movies DESC, avg_rating DESC
LIMIT 30

title: The Eternal Teenager
description: Actors appearing in movies released when they were at least 80 years old, according to recorded birth and release years.
sql:
SELECT p.name, t.primary_title, t.premiered AS movie_year, p.born AS birth_year, t.premiered - p.born AS age_at_release, r.rating
FROM crew c JOIN people p ON p.person_id = c.person_id JOIN titles t ON t.title_id = c.title_id JOIN ratings r ON r.title_id = t.title_id
WHERE c.category IN ('actor', 'actress') AND t.type = 'movie' AND p.born IS NOT NULL AND t.premiered IS NOT NULL AND t.premiered - p.born >= 80 AND r.votes >= 1000
ORDER BY age_at_release DESC, r.votes DESC
LIMIT 30

title: The Shortest Movies with the Biggest Reputations
description: Movies no longer than 45 minutes that still attracted at least 10,000 votes, ranked by vote count.
sql:
SELECT t.primary_title, t.premiered AS year, t.runtime_minutes, r.rating, r.votes
FROM titles t JOIN ratings r ON r.title_id = t.title_id
WHERE t.type = 'movie' AND t.runtime_minutes BETWEEN 1 AND 45 AND r.votes >= 10000
ORDER BY r.votes DESC, r.rating DESC
LIMIT 30

title: The Actors Who Have Been Around Forever
description: Actors whose rated movie appearances span the longest period, requiring at least 10 movies with 1,000+ votes.
sql:
SELECT p.name, MIN(t.premiered) AS first_movie, MAX(t.premiered) AS last_movie, MAX(t.premiered) - MIN(t.premiered) AS career_span, COUNT(DISTINCT t.title_id) AS movies
FROM crew c JOIN people p ON p.person_id = c.person_id JOIN titles t ON t.title_id = c.title_id JOIN ratings r ON r.title_id = t.title_id
WHERE c.category IN ('actor', 'actress') AND t.type = 'movie' AND t.premiered IS NOT NULL AND r.votes >= 1000
GROUP BY p.person_id
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t.title_id) >= 10
ORDER BY career_span DESC, movies DESC
LIMIT 30

title: The Genre Chameleons
description: Actors with credits in the widest variety of movie genres, counting distinct comma-separated genres from the titles view. Requires SQLite JSON support.
sql:
WITH actor_genres AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT c.person_id, TRIM(g.value) AS genre
  FROM crew c JOIN titles t ON t.title_id = c.title_id JOIN ratings r ON r.title_id = t.title_id
  JOIN json_each('["' || REPLACE(COALESCE(t.genres, ''), ',', '","') || '"]') g
  WHERE c.category IN ('actor', 'actress') AND t.type = 'movie' AND r.votes >= 1000 AND TRIM(g.value) <> '' AND t.genres <> 'N/A'
)
SELECT p.name, COUNT(*) AS different_genres, GROUP_CONCAT(genre, ', ') AS genres
FROM actor_genres ag JOIN people p ON p.person_id = ag.person_id
GROUP BY ag.person_id
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 10
ORDER BY different_genres DESC, p.name
LIMIT 30

title: The TV Series That Refuses to Die
description: TV series with the longest span between recorded start and end years. Only titles with both years recorded are included.
sql:
SELECT t.primary_title, t.premiered AS start_year, t.ended AS end_year, t.ended - t.premiered AS years_running, r.rating, r.votes
FROM titles t JOIN ratings r ON r.title_id = t.title_id
WHERE t.type = 'tvSeries' AND t.premiered IS NOT NULL AND t.ended IS NOT NULL AND t.ended >= t.premiered
ORDER BY years_running DESC, r.votes DESC
LIMIT 30

title: The Actor Pair That Keeps Reuniting
description: Pairs of actors who appear together in at least five movies with 25,000+ votes.
sql:
WITH appearances AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT c.title_id, c.person_id
  FROM crew c JOIN titles t ON t.title_id = c.title_id JOIN ratings r ON r.title_id = t.title_id
  WHERE c.category IN ('actor', 'actress') AND t.type = 'movie' AND r.votes >= 25000
)
SELECT p1.name AS actor_1, p2.name AS actor_2, COUNT(*) AS movies_together
FROM appearances a JOIN appearances b ON b.title_id = a.title_id AND b.person_id > a.person_id
JOIN people p1 ON p1.person_id = a.person_id JOIN people p2 ON p2.person_id = b.person_id
GROUP BY a.person_id, b.person_id
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5
ORDER BY movies_together DESC
LIMIT 30

title: The Director Whose Movies Get Worse with Age
description: Directors with at least eight well-known movies, comparing average ratings in the earlier and later halves of their release-ordered filmography.
sql:
WITH films AS (
  SELECT c.person_id, t.premiered, r.rating,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY c.person_id ORDER BY t.premiered, t.title_id) AS rn,
         COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY c.person_id) AS total
  FROM crew c JOIN titles t ON t.title_id = c.title_id JOIN ratings r ON r.title_id = t.title_id
  WHERE c.category = 'director' AND t.type = 'movie' AND t.premiered IS NOT NULL AND r.votes >= 5000
), halves AS (
  SELECT person_id,
         AVG(CASE WHEN rn <= total / 2.0 THEN rating END) AS early_avg,
         AVG(CASE WHEN rn > total / 2.0 THEN rating END) AS late_avg,
         MAX(total) AS movies
  FROM films GROUP BY person_id
)
SELECT p.name, h.movies, ROUND(h.early_avg, 2) AS early_avg, ROUND(h.late_avg, 2) AS late_avg, ROUND(h.late_avg - h.early_avg, 2) AS rating_change
FROM halves h JOIN people p ON p.person_id = h.person_id
WHERE h.movies >= 8 AND h.early_avg IS NOT NULL AND h.late_avg IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY rating_change ASC
LIMIT 30

title: The Most Misleading Movie Titles
description: Movies sharing a title but released in different years, ranked by the largest difference in IMDb rating. Shared titles do not prove a remake relationship.
sql:
SELECT a.primary_title, a.premiered AS year_1, ra.rating AS rating_1, b.premiered AS year_2, rb.rating AS rating_2, ROUND(ABS(ra.rating - rb.rating), 2) AS rating_gap
FROM titles a JOIN titles b ON LOWER(a.primary_title) = LOWER(b.primary_title) AND a.title_id < b.title_id AND a.premiered IS NOT NULL AND b.premiered IS NOT NULL AND a.premiered <> b.premiered
JOIN ratings ra ON ra.title_id = a.title_id JOIN ratings rb ON rb.title_id = b.title_id
WHERE a.type = 'movie' AND b.type = 'movie' AND ra.votes >= 5000 AND rb.votes >= 5000
ORDER BY rating_gap DESC
LIMIT 30

title: The Most Unproductive Movie Decade for an Actor
description: Actor-decade combinations with the lowest average ratings, requiring at least five movies with 1,000+ votes in that decade.
sql:
SELECT p.name, (t.premiered / 10) * 10 AS decade, COUNT(DISTINCT t.title_id) AS movies, ROUND(AVG(r.rating), 2) AS avg_rating
FROM crew c JOIN people p ON p.person_id = c.person_id JOIN titles t ON t.title_id = c.title_id JOIN ratings r ON r.title_id = t.title_id
WHERE c.category IN ('actor', 'actress') AND t.type = 'movie' AND t.premiered IS NOT NULL AND r.votes >= 1000
GROUP BY c.person_id, (t.premiered / 10) * 10
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t.title_id) >= 5
ORDER BY avg_rating ASC, movies DESC
LIMIT 30

title: The Most Confusing Person in IMDb
description: People credited in the widest variety of IMDb principal-credit categories, with their number of distinct credited titles.
sql:
SELECT p.name, COUNT(DISTINCT c.category) AS categories, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT c.category) AS jobs, COUNT(DISTINCT c.title_id) AS credited_titles
FROM crew c JOIN people p ON p.person_id = c.person_id
GROUP BY c.person_id
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT c.category) >= 5
ORDER BY categories DESC, credited_titles DESC
LIMIT 30
